## Jahmyr Gibbs

**Role.** Gibbs is the clear lead back in Detroit. He played 77% of snaps on the season and 76% over the last 4. His opportunity share is 44% on the season and 47% over the last 4 (up 3). His carry share is 77% on the season and 73% over the last 4.

**Volume.** Carries went from 22.1 per game on the season to 24.3 over the last 4. That is 28.5 carries plus targets per game.

**Scoring chances.** He has 44 red-zone carries on the season, 23 of them in the last 4 (6.5 per game). He has 15 goal-line carries, 7 in the last 4 (1.8 per game). He has no goal-line targets. His 9 rushing TDs lead this pair.

**Efficiency.** He averages 4.8 yards per carry. Last 4 he's at 5.1 yards per carry and 123.5 rushing yards per game. His receiving is thin: 6.3 yards per target on the season, 5.8 over the last 4. Targets are 5.6 per game on the season but 4.3 over the last 4, and he had zero catches on his only target in Week 9. He has 2 lost fumbles, 1 of them in the last 4.

**Injury.** Stat Hub lists him as healthy. My two web searches turned up nothing for 2026: the results were old hamstring stories from earlier seasons. I couldn't verify a Week 10 practice report, so I'm not claiming one. Hamstring strains, the injury type that shows up in his history, tend to cost 1–3 games and re-aggravate often if the player returns early. A limited Wednesday practice would be a modest warning sign, but none is confirmed.

**Teammates.** Sione Vaki is the only other back with real work: 10% opportunity share over the last 4, 3 targets, 0 red-zone and 0 goal-line touches. Jacob Saylors is out with a neck injury, and Jabari Small has 3% of snaps. Nobody threatens the goal-line role.

**Context.** Detroit won 19-9, a low-scoring game. The game against NE is in Germany, a neutral-site trip that doesn't change his usage.

## Kenneth Walker III

**Role.** Walker played 74% of snaps on the season and 74% over the last 4. His opportunity share is 42% on the season and 39% over the last 4 (down 3). His carry share is 74% on the season and 73% over the last 4.

**Volume.** He gets 19.9 carries per game on the season, but 18.0 over the last 4. That is 22.3 carries plus targets per game over the last 4, about 6 fewer than Gibbs.

**Scoring chances.** He has 34 red-zone carries on the season, 15 in the last 4 (4.8 per game with targets). He has 15 goal-line carries, 7 in the last 4 (1.8 per game), the same goal-line volume as Gibbs. He also has 2 goal-line targets on the season. His TDs are 7 rushing and 4 receiving. Scoring 4 times through the air from a 4.5-target-per-game role is above what that role normally produces, so some of it is likely to fade.

**Efficiency.** He averages 5.5 yards per carry, the best of the two. Over the last 4 that's 4.7. His receiving production is thinner than his TD total suggests: 4.8 yards per target on the season and 5.2 over the last 4. He has 0 lost fumbles.

**Injury.** Stat Hub lists him as healthy. My search found only August 2026 items (a swollen ankle that Andy Reid tied to a shoe issue, which cost him the preseason finale). Nothing I found shows a Week 10 designation, so I can't confirm it. The Chiefs' injury report will settle it.

**Teammates.** Emmett Johnson is the real threat to his share. Johnson has 11 targets over the last 4, ahead of Walker's 17 only slightly in context, and 4 red-zone touches over the last 4. He holds 9% of opportunities and 26% of snaps. Brashard Smith is on IR with a hamstring, and Ben VanSumeren is out. The news feed also flags a rookie backup overshadowing Walker in the Week 8 loss.

## Head to head

| | Gibbs | Walker |
|---|---|---|
| Points per game (season / last 4) | 24.0 / 21.8 | 22.9 / 19.8 |
| Carries per game (last 4) | 24.3 | 18.0 |
| Opportunity share (last 4) | 47% | 39% |
| Red-zone carries (season) | 44 | 34 |
| Goal-line carries | 15 | 15 |
| Yards per carry (season) | 4.8 | 5.5 |
| Range (floor / ceiling) | 14.2 / 31.4 | 15.3 / 33.8 |

**Volume.** Gibbs, clearly. His opportunity share rose 3 points while Walker's fell 3, and the gap is now 47% to 39%.

**Touchdown role.** The goal-line carries are even at 15 each, but Gibbs has 10 more red-zone carries and 9 rushing TDs to Walker's 7. Walker's 4 receiving TDs are the less sustainable part.

**Efficiency.** Walker wins per carry (5.5 vs 4.8). That only matters when the volume is there, and Gibbs has more of it.

**Rest of season.** Stat Hub projects Gibbs at 211.5 points through Week 18 and Walker at 183.3, a 28-point gap. Schedule ease is 0.97 for Gibbs and 1.00 for Walker. I don't have the Nth-easiest ranking for Weeks 15–17 for either, so I can't rank the playoff weeks.

**Floor vs ceiling.** Walker's range (15.3 / 33.8) is slightly higher at both ends, but Gibbs's 14.2 floor sits on a much bigger workload.

**Injury risk.** Both are listed healthy. Gibbs carries more touches (28.5 vs 22.3 per game), which is more wear, but I found no confirmed issue for either.

## This week

Walker projects slightly higher at 21.5 against Gibbs at 20.9. The gap comes from the matchups.

- **Gibbs vs NE** is the 6th toughest RB matchup. New England allows 17.1 half-PPR points per game to RBs against a league average of 19.6, and the matchup multiplier is ×0.94.
- **Walker @ ATL** is the 8th easiest RB matchup. Atlanta allows 22.2 points per game to RBs, and the multiplier is ×1.07.

Expert consensus has Walker at RB1 (FantasyPros RB1, RotoWire RB3, ESPN RB1) at 20.9. For Gibbs it is RB2 (FantasyPros RB2, RotoWire RB1, ESPN RB2) at 20.7. A 0.6-point gap is noise. I lean Walker by a hair this week, mainly for the matchup and his higher ceiling, but this is a coin flip. If you can only start one, either is fine; don't bench the other for any reason except a confirmed injury.

## The verdict

**Gibbs rest of season.** I'd rather have him: 47% opportunity share, 24.3 carries per game, the larger red-zone volume, and a 28-point projected gap through Week 18. Confidence is moderate to high. This week's matchup is a one-week effect, and his volume carries over every week.

**What would flip it:**
- A Gibbs injury designation, particularly a hamstring that keeps him limited in practice.
- Emmett Johnson's targets and red-zone touches growing into more of Walker's share, which would hurt Walker, not help him.
- Detroit's offense stalling in low-scoring games like the 19-9 win, which caps TD upside.
- Walker's opportunity share recovering toward 42% or higher, which would narrow the gap.

I couldn't verify either player's Week 10 injury status from my searches. Check the Wednesday and Thursday practice reports before locking in lineups.
